headline: ASML, the Dutch maker of the machines that print advanced computer chips, raised the low end of its 2026 sales forecast and warned it cannot fully meet customer demand in 2027 and 2028.
score_reason: Pool 7 kept: ASML's results are a main gauge of AI chip demand; the lead was read in Bloomberg and the figures in Anadolu's full report.
importance_line: What changed is that the only maker of the extreme ultraviolet machines used for the most advanced chips says AI demand will outrun its supply through 2028, which matters first to the people and firms waiting on AI chips and devices, then to chipmakers such as TSMC and Samsung that compete for ASML's tools, then to ASML's shareholders, and the doubt is that sales came in slightly below expectations and the interest in 2029 and 2030 is customer interest, not orders.
summary: Bloomberg reports that ASML Holding, the Dutch maker of chip-making machines, boosted its 2026 sales forecast on Wednesday 14 Oct 2026 but warned that soaring AI spending leaves it facing a possible supply shortfall in the next two years, with chief executive Christophe Fouquet saying "Customers are asking us every single day to get more tools." Anadolu Agency adds that the new 2026 range is €44 billion to €45 billion, up from €43 billion to €45 billion, that third-quarter net profit of €4.96 billion beat analysts' expectations while net sales of €11.66 billion were slightly below them, and that some customers are already asking about orders for 2029 and 2030, and that ASML, the world's only producer of the extreme ultraviolet lithography machines used for the most advanced chips, is studying more capacity for 2028 beyond the 30% increase it announced earlier.
notes: Bloomberg is paywalled after two paragraphs; figures from Anadolu Agency's full report. Share-price reaction not used (conflicting headlines, not read).
